dataset.name: Geochemical characterization of floodplain sediments from Meander C and O in the East River Watershed, CO, USA
description: This data package is part of the Watershed Function SFA data collection and contains geochemical characterization of sediments as a function of depth in the pumphouse vicinity, including Meander C and Meander O (oxbow). This data was used in the manuscript "Fox, P.M., Bill, M., Heckman, K., Conrad, M., Anderson, C., Keiluweit, M., and Nico, P.S.Shale as a Source of Organic Carbon in Floodplain Sediments of a Mountainous Watershed" published in Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences. Data includes sieving, total organic carbon (TOC), total inorganic carbon (TIC), total nitrogen (TN), carbon isotopes (14C and 13C) of whole sediment. Sediment density fractionation data is also included, with measurements of TOC, TN, 14C and 13C on density fractions. Metal and carbon concentrations from various sediment extractions (HCl, dithionite, oxalate, water, and pyrophosphate) are included. Characterization of extracted carbon by fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and UV-Visible light spectroscopy. Characterization of density fractionated (light fractions) organic carbon by FTIR. Carbon X-ray spectroscopy (C near edge X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy [NEXAFS] and scanning transmission X-ray microscopy [STXM]) is also included for shale samples and sediment samples.

3. Radiocarbon analysis was supported in part by the Radiocarbon Collaborative, which is jointly sponsored by the USDA Forest Service Northern Research Station, the KCCAMS Facility at UC Irvine, and Michigan Technological University.

spatialCoverage.description: The East River (ER) is a snow‐dominated, headwater basin of the Upper Colorado River Basin (UCRB) located in the western United States. The ER is the designated testbed of Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's Watershed Function Scientific Focus Area (WFSFA). Through WFSFA, observational networks have been established to measure stream discharge and precipitation chemistry.The ER is considered representative of many snow‐dominated headwaters of the Rocky Mountains. The study domain encompasses nearly 85 square km, a 1.4‐km vertical drop in elevation (4,120 to 2,760 m) and pristine alpine, subalpine, montane, and riparian ecosystems. The ER contains high‐energy mountain streams to low‐energy meandering floodplains and is eroding primarily into the Cretaceous, carbon‐rich, marine shale of the Mancos Formation.

measurementTechnique:
Methods are described in individual readme files for each data type and in the associated journal publication. Descriptions are also provided here.
SUVA Data:
All data was collected using a Thermo Aquamate Plus UV-Vis spectrophotometer using a 1-cm quartz cell. NaCl whole samples were run un-diluted, while PP-SPE samples were diluted 40x with MilliQ water. The baseline was zeroed on a MilliQ water blank prior to collecting sample spectra. All data was corrected for dilution, converted to m-1 by multiplying by 100, and divided by the DOC concentration in mg/L to convert the raw absorbance values to specific absorbance in units of L/mg-m.
See 'summary of sediment data_Fox et al 2018.xlsx' file to identify individual sample names (depths, GPS locations).

C NEXAFS and STXM Data:
C_NEXAFS data_shale.csv contains bulk carbon NEXAFS data for shale samples collected from PLM6 (weathered and unweathered) and GRO (top, middle, bottom).
C_STXM data_sediment.csv contains C STXM data for floodplain sediment samples collected from the cut-bank (MC-1) and middle (MC-3) of meander C. Data was collected at several spots (or particles) for each sample. The cores were collected at the location of the MCT2 transect wells.
Both normalized data and data fits are presented.

FTIR Data:
FTIR data_FLF_OLF.csv contains data for organic fractions from density separations (FLF=free light fraction, OLF=occluded light fraction).
FTIR data _HCl-SPE_PP-SPE_PP-1kD.csv contains data for organic matter extracted (by 0.5 M HCl or 0.1 M sodium pyrophosphate) from sediments and purified through solid-phase extraction (SPE) or dialysis (1kD).
All data was collected by ATR-FTIR (Thermo Scientific Nicolet iS50) equipped with a quartz crystal. All data was collected with a liquid nitrogen cooled MCT/A detector. Atmospheric suppression, ATR-correction, baseline correction, and intensity normalization were performed on background-corrected sample spectra using OMNIC software. The corrected and normalized spectra are given here.
See 'summary of sediment data_Fox et al 2018.xlsx' file to identify individual sample names (depths, GPS locations).
